sn51.13:1.2: The basic statement includes a long compound (chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṁ), which leaves the relationship between the terms ambiguous. This analysis clarifies that the first two terms have a dependent relationship, “immersion due to enthusiasm”.
sn51.13:1.7: This confirms that these two items of the compound belong together. Padhāna is a normal term for “effort, striving”, while saṅkhāra can mean “effective work” (SN 48.17:1.5). The explanation shows that the energy here is not just something that one has, but which is generated through the active exercise of the mind in the four duties of right effort.
